newsitem.title: USA: Compaq says Q2 outlook remains very strong.
newsitem.headline: Compaq says Q2 outlook remains very strong.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp Chief Financial Officer Earl Mason said Friday the world's largest personal computer maker had a "very good April and a very good May" and that Europe is "very, very strong."
Mason said Compaq continues to feel very bullish about its outlook for the second quarter, despite Intel Corp's profit warning earlier today.
Mason said he was comfortable with Wall Street's consensus estimate that Compaq will earn about $1.38/share for the quarter.
He declined comment on Intel's reduced outlook for its second quarter except to say that Compaq must be taking substantial market share away from other computer makers.

"I think we are taking substantial market share," Mason said. "So someone might be having a problem." He declined to comment further or to speculate on which PC maker might be having problems that might be spilling over onto Intel.

"Our order growth is well above that of the marketplace," Mason said in a telephone interview. "We just feel very good about the quarter and we feel very bullish about the outlook for the second quarter and the rest of the year."
Earlier today Intel said weaker-than-anticipated demand, especially in Europe, was expected to cause revenue and net income for the second quarter to fall below expectations.
Mason said he is comfortable with Wall Street's forecast of second quarter revenues for Compaq of about $5 billion.
"We are very comfortable with all that," he said.
Compaq's shares soared 4-1/8 to 105-7/8 in active trading after falling to an intra-session low of 97-3/4 earlier.
